questions.prompt: Which residual plot supports the model?
options: A smooth sine-like curve
A long run of positive values then negative values
Spread growing with the signal
Random scatter around zero with constant spread
questions.explanation: Structure in residuals signals a problem; scatter is what noise looks like.

What fraction (percent, 1 decimal) of the final value is reached at t=2*tau?
sigma_hat=0.12 and sqrt((J^T J)^-1) for tau = 0.35. SE of tau in milliseconds (nearest integer)?
With SE(tau)=0.042 s and t critical value 2.101, the 95% half-width in milliseconds (nearest integer)?
40 points, 3 parameters, SSR=0.37. sigma_hat in rad/s (3 decimals)?
Two fits of tau, one in seconds and one in milliseconds, with the same bounds numbers (1e-3, 10) will
options: give identical optima, as the bounds are only a starting search range
restrict the millisecond fit to physically unreasonable values
always converge faster, as the smaller numbers are better conditioned
be equivalent, because the unit change cancels in the optimizer
questions.explanation: Bounds expressed in the wrong unit change the problem.

questions.prompt: A fit with u=0 returns a gain K identical to the initial guess because
options: the bounds forced K to stay equal to the initial value
solve_ivp ignores K and uses a default gain inside the model

questions.prompt: Fitting ln(tau) instead of tau is helpful because
options: it keeps tau positive and makes errors relative
it removes the need for a model to be fitted
it moves the optimum to a better value
it makes the measurement noise Gaussian
questions.explanation: Unconstrained optimization on log scale; SE(ln tau)~SE(tau)/tau.

Describe the outputs and metadata you would save so that a colleague can reproduce and audit a parameter fit months later.

questions.prompt: The simulator uses rtol=1e-3 while your measurement noise is 0.1 rad/s on a 6 rad/s signal. Explain why this can still hurt a least-squares fit and how you would test the effect.
rubric: Explains that finite-difference Jacobians amplify small, nonsmooth simulator errors.
Proposes tightening rtol/atol and compare fits.
Checks the simulator against an analytic solution and monitors optimizer status.

questions.prompt: Gauss-Newton (here Newton) for tanh(x)=0 uses x ← x - sinh(x)cosh(x). It converges from x0=0.95 and diverges from x0=1.15. At which positive x_c does the iteration map x_c to -x_c, separating the two behaviours? Give 3 decimals.
questions.explanation: The iteration is x ← x - ½ sinh(2x). Requiring x_c - ½ sinh(2x_c) = -x_c gives sinh(2x_c) = 4x_c. The positive root is x_c = 1.08866. For |x0| < x_c the map contracts to 0 (0.95 gives -0.684, 0.234, -0.0087, ...), for |x0| > x_c each step overshoots farther (1.15 gives -1.318, 2.156, -16.5, ...) because ½ sinh(2x) grows faster than 2x.

questions.skillLabel: Standard error along a singular direction
questions.prompt: At the optimum of a two-parameter fit, the Jacobian has singular values 12.87 and 1.865, and the noise estimate is σ̂ = 0.1. What is the standard error of the worst-determined combination of parameters (the direction of the smaller singular value)? Give 3 decimals.
questions.explanation: Cov = σ̂²(JᵀJ)⁻¹ = σ̂² V Σ⁻² Vᵀ. Along the right singular vector v_i the standard deviation is σ̂/σ_i. For σ_min = 1.865: 0.1/1.865 = 0.0536 (about 0.054). For σ_max = 12.87 it would be 0.1/12.87 = 0.0078, so the combination along the weak direction is nearly 7 times less well determined.

questions.prompt: A Levenberg-Marquardt fit of a time constant barely moves it when you switch its unit from seconds to milliseconds, even though the data and model are the same. What is the right fix?
options: Increase the damping λ until the step becomes small enough to stay inside the trust region.
Run the same fit in float64 only, since float32 rounding of the milliseconds value is what causes the stall.
Give τ a suitable x_scale (or non-dimensionalize it) so steps in all variables affect the cost comparably.
Remove the bounds on τ so the optimizer is free to take longer steps in that variable.
questions.explanation: The LM step solves (JᵀJ + λI)δ = -Jᵀr. In milliseconds the τ column of J is 1000 times smaller, so its squared singular value falls far below λ and that direction is heavily damped: the step in τ is almost frozen (in the lesson's check the change in τ drops from -1.40 s to -7e-6 s for λ = 1). The penalty λ‖δ‖² compares quantities in different units. The remedy is to scale the variables (x_scale of the order of each parameter, or 'jac', or non-dimensionalizing) so the trust region matches each variable's natural size. Raising λ makes it worse, precision is not the cause, and removing bounds does not change the damping.
